PARALLEL:
---
name: parallel-search
description: Web search, page extraction, deep research and data enrichment via the Parallel API (`parallel-cli`). Use for current events, docs lookups, fact-checking, content extraction, and multi-source research.
---

## Setup

`parallel-cli` (the official [Parallel Web Systems](https://parallel.ai) CLI)
is installed on PATH. Authentication is declarative: the wrapper exports
`PARALLEL_API_KEY` from the sops secret `/run/secrets/parallel_api_key`, so the
CLI is always authenticated — no `parallel-cli login` and no config edits.
Check with `parallel-cli auth` if in doubt.

This replaces the old Brave `bx` CLI and the `brave-search` MCP server. For
fetching pages prefer `parallel-cli extract` first; fall back to the
`agent-browser` skill only for pages that need a logged-in browser session
(dashboard, paywall, JS-heavy interactive sites).

## Commands that matter to agents

Always pass `--json` for structured output and pipe through `jq`.

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| Fast keyword/lookup search | `parallel-cli search "query" --mode turbo --json` |
| High-quality search (recommended default) | `parallel-cli search "query" --mode fast --json` |
| Extended snippets per result | `parallel-cli search "query" --json` (default mode `basic`) |
| Deep search | `parallel-cli search "query" --mode advanced --json` |
| Domain-restricted search | `parallel-cli search "query" --include-domains docs.rs,github.com --json` |
| Fresh results only | `parallel-cli search "query" --after-date 2026-01-01 --json` |
| Extract a URL to markdown | `parallel-cli extract https://example.com --json` |
| Extract focused on a goal | `parallel-cli extract https://example.com --objective "pricing" --json` |
| Full page content | `parallel-cli extract https://example.com --full-content --json` |
| Deep research report | `parallel-cli research run "question" --processor pro --json` |
| Bulk entity discovery | `parallel-cli findall entity-search "AI startups in SF" --entity-type companies -n 25 --json` |
| Recall earlier research | `parallel-cli memory retrieve --query "topic" --json` |

Useful `search` flags: `--max-results N`, `--exclude-domains`, `--location`
(ISO country code), `--excerpt-max-chars-total N` (CLI default 60,000 — the
excerpts are already dense and token-efficient; prefer them over fetching
every URL).

---
name: knowledge-base
description: >
  Look up and update the user's single private knowledge-base repo
  (github.com/skyne98/knowledge-base). Every research topic is a subdirectory
  with its own README (synthesis) + sources/ (evidence); the repo root holds a
  central index (README.md + INDEX.md). Use this skill at the start of any
  research task to check for an existing topic, and at the end of a research
  session to record findings (clone → update topic + index → push).
---

# knowledge-base — `skyne98/knowledge-base`

The user keeps **one private knowledge-base repo** on GitHub:
`skyne98/knowledge-base`. It is the canonical, persistent record of research
gathered across agent sessions. Every topic is a **subdirectory**; the repo
root is the central index. The old per-topic `kb-<topic>` repos are **deleted from
GitHub** (bare-clone backups live in `~/Project/kb-archived-backups`) — never
create, push to, or resurrect them.

> **Privacy invariant:** `skyne98/knowledge-base` must always be **PRIVATE**.
> Never change it to public or internal visibility. After creation or any
> visibility-affecting operation, explicitly verify `isPrivate: true`.

Full convention documented in `~/nixos/docs/knowledge-base-repos.md`.

---

## When to use this skill

- **Start of a research task** — clone the repo and read the root `README.md`
  (topic index). If a topic already exists, read `<topic>/README.md` and
  `<topic>/sources/INDEX.md` *before* doing fresh research, so you build on
  prior work instead of redoing it.
- **End of a research session** — record what you gathered: clone the repo (or
  `cd` if already cloned), update the topic's `README.md` synthesis + add
  primary sources under `<topic>/sources/`, commit, and push.

## 1. Find an existing topic

```bash
gh repo clone skyne98/knowledge-base ~/Project/knowledge-base
cd ~/Project/knowledge-base
# The central index — table of every topic with a one-line description
sed -n '/## Index/,/## Structure/p' README.md
# Or the machine-readable manifest: topic<TAB>path<TAB>description
cat INDEX.md
```

## 2. Standard repo structure

```
knowledge-base/
├── README.md      # Central index — table of all topics
├── INDEX.md       # Machine-readable manifest (topic, path, description)
└── <topic>/       # One directory per topic
    ├── README.md  # Synthesized dossier — the readable summary
    └── sources/   # Full-text primary sources + deep dives
        ├── INDEX.md         # Manifest of all gathered sources wi
